chunks: And it was narrated from Murāzim ibn Ḥakīm al-Azdī that he said:

I had been ill for four months and did not perform any nāfilah prayer during them, so I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Indeed, I was ill for four months and did not perform any nāfilah prayer. So he said:
There is no making up required upon you. Indeed, the sick person is not like the healthy one. Whatever Allah has caused to overcome him, then Allah is more entitled to excuse him in it.

key_terms.الصَّحِيحِ: the healthy person, contrasted here with the sick
key_terms.الْعُذْرِ: excuse recognized and accepted in the legal and devotional sense
key_terms.الْمَرِيضَ: the sick person, whose condition affects legal responsibility
key_terms.غَلَبَ: overcame or overtook, referring to a state beyond one’s control
key_terms.قَضَاءٌ: making up a missed act of worship after its time has passed
key_terms.نَافِلَةً: supererogatory prayer beyond the obligatory salat

ai.seo_question: Does a sick person have to make up missed nāfilah prayers in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that a sick person who misses nāfilah prayers during illness is not required to make them up. It emphasizes that illness constitutes a valid excuse, and that what overcomes a person by Allah’s decree is treated with divine leniency.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1430 - Murazim ibn Hakim al-Azdi narrated that He said:

"I was ill for four months and did not perform any of the supererogatory (nafilah) prayers during that time. I mentioned this to Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as)
Imam (as) said: 'There is no obligation on you to make them up; indeed, the condition of the sick is not like that of the healthy. Whatever overwhelms you, Allah (swt) is more deserving of offering an excuse for it.'".
